payload.goal: Create a small Kotlin utility that validates the format of an Android Enterprise enrollment token, plus unit tests.
assumptions: The token is a string (e.g., from a QR code or manual entry) that must be validated for format only, not for cryptographic authenticity or server-side validity.

tasks.title: Define token validation rules
tasks.description: Specify the accepted format: non-blank, trimmed length within a defined min/max range, and characters limited to the base64url alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-', '_') with optional padding '=' only at the end. Document these rules as constants.
acceptance_criteria: Rules are documented as named constants (min/max length, allowed charset).
Padding '=' is only permitted at the end of the token.

tasks.title: Implement EnrollmentTokenValidator
tasks.description: Create a Kotlin object or class exposing a function isValid(token: String?): Boolean (and optionally a Result-returning variant) that applies the rules from task 1 without throwing on null or malformed input.
acceptance_criteria: Null and blank input return false.
Tokens with invalid characters return false.
Tokens with '=' not at the end return false.
Tokens outside length bounds return false.
Valid base64url tokens within bounds return true.

tasks.title: Add unit tests
tasks.description: Write JUnit tests covering: null/blank, too short, too long, invalid characters (e.g., '+', '/', spaces), misplaced padding, valid minimal token, valid maximal token, and a realistic sample token.
acceptance_criteria: All test cases pass.
Tests cover both positive and negative paths including edge lengths and padding placement.

risks: Treating format validity as proof of authenticity: a well-formed token may still be expired, revoked, or invalid server-side; the utility must be documented as format-only.

payload.summary: Create a Kotlin utility that validates the format of an Android Enterprise enrollment token, plus JUnit tests. The implementation treats the token as a format-only check (base64url charset, length bounds, trailing '=' padding), never logs token contents, returns typed results without throwing, and uses synthetic test tokens only.

The implementation is clean, deterministic, framework-free, and well-tested, but it contains a correctness bug in padding validation that causes valid base64url tokens with trailing padding to be rejected, and the build/test verification could not be executed (no Gradle wrapper present).

issues.description: The padding validation logic is incorrect. After the MisplacedPadding check, the character loop validates against BASE64URL_CHARS, which excludes '='. This means a token with a single trailing '=' (e.g., the 'valid token with trailing padding' test case) will hit the '=' character in the loop, fail the `ch !in BASE64URL_CHARS` check, and return InvalidCharacters instead of Valid. The trailing-padding test would fail, and legitimate padded base64url tokens would be rejected.
issues.recommendation: Exclude the trailing padding character from the character-set loop, or validate the non-padding portion separately. For example, iterate over `trimmed.dropLast(1)` when the last character is '=', or check `ch !in ALLOWED_CHARS` after confirming padding is only at the end. Also add a test for multiple trailing '=' characters to clarify intended behavior (base64url typically uses at most two padding chars).

issues.description: No Gradle wrapper (gradlew/gradlew.bat) is present in the workspace, and the `gradle` command is not available on the environment, so `gradle test` / `./gradlew test` both fail with 'No such file or directory'. The test suite cannot be executed to confirm it passes.
issues.recommendation: Add the Gradle wrapper (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar and .properties) so tests can be run reproducibly, or document the required Gradle installation. Re-run the test suite to confirm all tests pass after fixing the padding bug.

issues.description: The ALLOWED_CHARS constant is declared but never used, and the padding rule only permits a single trailing '=' (indexOf('=') must equal length-1). Standard base64url padding can be '=' or '=='. The current logic would treat '==' as MisplacedPadding because indexOf('=') returns the first '=' which is not the last character.
issues.recommendation: Either document that only a single trailing '=' is permitted, or adjust the padding rule to allow one or two trailing '=' characters (e.g., ensure all '=' characters are contiguous at the end). Remove the unused ALLOWED_CHARS constant or use it in the validation loop.

required_fixes: Fix the padding validation so that a token with trailing '=' padding is accepted (the character loop currently rejects '=').
Clarify and correctly handle base64url padding (single vs. double '=') and remove or use the unused ALLOWED_CHARS constant.
Add the Gradle wrapper (or otherwise enable test execution) and re-run the test suite to confirm all tests pass.

payload.summary: Fix the padding validation bug in EnrollmentTokenValidator so trailing '=' padding is accepted, correctly handle single/double '=' padding, remove the unused ALLOWED_CHARS constant, and add a Gradle wrapper so tests can be run reproducibly.

issues.recommendation: Clarify and document the separator rules; consider rejecting an empty prefix (e.g., a token starting with '#' or ':') and validating the prefix against a safe character set if a prefix is present.
